How attribute boosts work in Pathfinder 2e

Pathfinder's Remaster has no ability scores to roll or buy. Every attribute modifier starts at +0, each boost adds 1, and a flaw takes 1 away. You get four sets of boosts at 1st level, and within one set you can't boost the same attribute twice. That's how a new character reaches +4 in their key attribute and no higher.

The four sets at 1st level

  • Ancestry: most ancestries give two fixed boosts, one free boost, and a flaw (an elf boosts Dexterity and Intelligence, takes a free boost, and has a Constitution flaw). Humans and orcs get two free boosts; tengu get Dexterity and one free boost. Any ancestry can trade all of that for two free boosts and no flaw.
  • Background: two boosts. One is a choice of two attributes, the other is free.
  • Class: one boost to your key attribute. Some classes give a choice (a fighter picks Strength or Dexterity), and a rogue's racket adds its own.
  • Four free boosts to four different attributes.

Boosts at levels 5, 10, 15, and 20

Each of these levels gives four more free boosts, again to four different attributes. Below +4 a boost adds 1 as usual. Once an attribute is +4 or higher, a boost there is partial: the first one does nothing you can see, and the second one adds 1. The calculator marks a waiting partial boost with ½.

Key attributeLevel 1Level 5Level 10Level 15Level 20
Boosted every time+4+4½+5+5½+6

An item of potency, apex items, and the like aren't counted here: they're gear, and the Character Builder leaves them to you too.

Works with

⚖️ Suggest Boosts fills every empty pick: your key attribute first, then Constitution, Dexterity, and Wisdom (for Hit Points, AC and Reflex, and Perception and Will), and at the later levels it skips attributes already at +4 apart from the key one. 🧝 Send to Character Builder starts a new character in the Character Builder with these picks, ready for its heritage, skills, feats, and gear. Then check its Strikes in the Attack Calculator.
